protocolMetadata.instructions: Finta is the user's bookkeeping. To upload bank or card transactions: parse the whole file yourself, compute its row count and net total, then call upload_transactions in chunks of up to 500 rows. Send every row, and mark rows you leave out with exclude. Resolve errors, warnings and open questions from the file and context. Ask the user only when you truly can't tell, and otherwise use the suggested defaults. When you're done, tell the user what was uploaded and what was left out. Tools marked "Not available to this company yet (early access: X)" belong to feature X, which this company doesn't have yet; that isn't a failure to report. Don't call them. If the user asks for something they do, say once that the feature isn't available to them yet and offer to request access; only if they agree, send one submit_feedback request per feature, not one per tool. Otherwise, when no Finta tool can do what the user asked, or a Finta tool fails unexpectedly or misleads you, report it with submit_feedback (reported_by: agent) without asking first, tell the user in one line, and carry on. Use submit_feedback too when the user wants to send Finta a question, feedback or bug. If submit_feedback itself fails, don't retry or report that; tell the user they can email support@finta.com.

tool.description:
Purpose: Invite someone to the company's Finta team with the access they should have. Finta emails them a link to join.
Not for: Changing a pending invitation's access (update_team_invitation) or sending its email again (resend_team_invitation). People who already joined; they're managed in the Finta web app.

tool.name: bulk_update_transactions
tool.title: Bulk update transactions
tool.description:
Purpose: Make the same change to many transactions at once, up to 5,000, chosen by txn_ IDs or by filters: such as recategorizing every AWS charge, or moving a quarter's accounting dates by a month.
Not for: Different changes for different transactions; call update_transaction for each. Changing future transactions; a rule does that.
Returns: The job: id, status (queued, processing, success or failed), matched_count (null until the transactions are selected), updated_count, and errors (a page of failures, each with transaction_id, code, param and message). The job is all or nothing: a failed job changes no transactions, and errors say why.
When to use: "Recategorize all our Gusto transactions as Payroll", "Set the department to Engineering on every GitHub charge this year".
Workflow: Preview the selection with search_transactions using the same filters, then confirm the change and how many transactions it touches with the user before calling. To change the transactions from one account or card, find them with search_transactions and pass their transaction_ids. Pass exactly one of transaction_ids or filters, plus updates. This tool waits about 20 seconds for the job; if status is still queued or processing, call again with only job_id to check on it. A failed job with more than one page of errors has errors.has_more; pass job_id with starting_after set to errors.next_cursor for the next page. Calling again with the same transaction_ids or filters and updates within an hour of the first call returns the job that call started instead of starting another, so a retry is safe; after that, the same request runs again and picks up transactions that match now. With accounting_shift, the same request returns the first job for 30 days after it finishes, so dates never move twice; if that job comes back when the user meant to shift again, tell them.
Rules: Filters all must match, and select transactions by their values before the update. Split transactions are never selected by filters, and naming one in transaction_ids fails the job. In updates, null clears department_id or spread, or restores the original accounting date; merchant and category_id can't be null; accounting_date and accounting_shift can't be used together.

tool.name: upload_transactions
tool.title: Upload transactions
tool.description:
Purpose: Add bank or credit card transactions from a file or pasted data to one Finta account.
Not for: Changing transactions already in Finta, or accounts that sync automatically unless the user confirms the sync is broken.
Returns: Validation for every row sent so far (errors, warnings, open_questions, ready_to_commit, next_step, summary in dollars), or the import result after a commit, including a url where the user can review or undo the upload.
When to use: "Add these transactions", "import this statement", "upload our Chase CSV".
Workflow: list_accounts, then create_account if no account matches, then call this tool with rows in chunks of up to 500, resolve what each result reports, and finish with commit: true once ready_to_commit is true. Nothing is visible in Finta until the commit. If the commit returns status importing, call again with only upload_id to check on it; that changes nothing.
Rules: Parse the whole file yourself and send every row, including rows you leave out, which you mark in exclude with a reason. Compute file_totals from the file itself. Pass dates exactly as the file writes them. Send amounts as plain signed decimals such as -45.00: convert accounting notation like (45.00) to -45.00 and drop currency symbols, but don't otherwise flip signs; if the file shows charges as positive, keep them and set sign_convention. Buying or selling investments doesn't change cash, so exclude those rows, but keep interest and dividends. Exclude a charge and its reversal together. Acknowledge a blocking warning only after checking the rows it lists, and mention acknowledged possible duplicates to the user. Answer open questions from the file and context, and ask the user only when you can't tell; otherwise use the suggested default. After committing, tell the user what was uploaded, what was left out and why, and give them the url.

Dates exactly as the file writes them, such as "03/04/2026", so Finta can work out month/day order. Descriptions of at most 40 characters; shorten longer ones to the merchant or payee. Amounts as plain signed decimals, such as "-45.00" for a file that writes "(45.00)".

tool.title: Get balance sheet
tool.description:
Purpose: Get the company's balance sheet as of one date: cash, assets, liabilities and equity.
Not for: Activity over a period, such as revenue or spending (get_income_statement) or cash movement (get_cash_flow). One section on its own; the full statement always comes back.
Returns: date is the exact inclusive cutoff used, with currency, refreshed_at, cash_cents, assets and liabilities (each with total_cents and categories), equity (total_cents, categories and retained_earnings), and liabilities_and_equity_cents, which equals assets.total_cents. Each category has category_id, name, balance_cents, position and parent_category_id. Amounts are integer cents, so divide by 100 for dollars.
When to use: "How much cash do we have?", "What were our total liabilities at the end of June?", "Show me the balance sheet".
Dates and source: Calendar dates use America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time); balances include all activity through the exact date. Whole months use whole-month rollups. A cutoff of today uses fresh current-month month-to-date (MTD) rollups for month-start through today. Other non-month-end cutoffs use slower raw-entry reads for just the cutoff month. Stale or unfilled MTD safely falls back to raw entries; reported balances are unchanged.
Freshness: refreshed_at covers the entire report through its exact cutoff. For rollup-only reads it is the maximum contributing rollup timestamp, including MTD. Any live raw portion is current as of the call, even when no raw entries match. It is null only when no contributing timestamp or live raw read is available.
Workflow: Omit date for today in Pacific Time. A parent category's amount already includes its children, so to total a section, add only the categories whose parent_category_id is null, or use the section's total_cents.

tool.name: get_category_total
tool.title: Get category total
tool.description:
Purpose: Get an exact total in one call: for a category and everything under it, or for one merchant, over an inclusive date range or as of an exact date. Or split that total in one call by merchant, ranked, or by month.
Not for: The whole income statement or balance sheet; the report tools return those. Listing individual transactions or entries; never add those up yourself for a total or a ranking.
Returns: Without group_by: total_cents, debit_cents, credit_cents, currency, point_in_time, the exact dates used and refreshed_at. With group_by: data, a list of rows, each with merchant (null for activity recorded without one) or month, and total_cents, debit_cents and credit_cents, plus the dates used, refreshed_at, has_more and next_cursor. Amounts are signed integer cents, so divide by 100 for dollars: assets are debits minus credits, and every other category is credits minus debits, so expenses come out negative. For a balance sheet category, each month row is cumulative through that month's closing date, with the last calendar month's cutoff at end_date, so never add month rows up for it.
When to use: "How much did we spend on software this year?", "What's our total for OpenAI, all time?", "Which vendors do we spend the most on?", "Who are our top 10 customers?", "What did we pay AWS each month?", "Which month did we spend the most?", "What was our accounts receivable balance at the end of June?"
Dates: All dates are calendar dates in America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time). Periodic totals include exactly start_date through end_date, inclusive; point-in-time totals include all activity through the exact date. This replaces the old behavior that ignored the day. For group_by month, periodic first and last rows are clipped to the exact range; point-in-time start_date selects the first displayed month without excluding earlier cumulative activity, and the last calendar month's cutoff is end_date. Whole months use whole-month rollups. Current-month start through today uses fresh month-to-date (MTD) rollups, so month-aligned month-to-date and year-to-date requests stay fast. Other partial months, including a midmonth start, use slower raw-entry reads for just those months. Stale or unfilled MTD safely falls back to raw entries.
Freshness: refreshed_at covers the whole total or returned page, including partial months, not only full months. For rollup-only reads it is the maximum contributing rollup timestamp, including MTD. Any live raw portion is current as of the call, even when no raw entries match. It is null only when no contributing timestamp or live raw read is available.
Workflow: Get category_id and point_in_time from list_categories. When point_in_time is false (income statement categories), pass start_date and end_date; when it's true (balance sheet categories), pass date only, except with group_by month, which always takes start_date and end_date. For vendors use the top-level Expenses category (parent_id null), and for customers the top-level Income category. group_by merchant ranks merchants: order desc, the default, puts the biggest first in the category's own direction (most spent under Expenses, most received under Income), and asc the smallest first; limit takes that many rows from the top, so limit 10 is a top 10. group_by month gives one row per month, up to 120 months, oldest first unless you set order. If has_more is true and you need more rows, call again with the same arguments and starting_after set to next_cursor, unchanged. Merchant names are exact as recorded, so one vendor can appear under several spellings: combine obvious variants and say you did. For one merchant's total, pass merchant, matching the name exactly, including case, from list_merchants or a group_by merchant row. If you don't know the exact spelling, find it with one search_transactions call using merchant and a small limit, then pass the name exactly as it appears there; the total still comes from this tool. Expenses and Income cover every category under them, but not purchases recorded as assets, such as capitalized equipment or the part of a prepaid plan not yet expensed, so a vendor's total can be less than what was paid; say so when it matters. For all time, start at the company's incorporation date from get_company and end today in Pacific Time. Use as few calls as the question needs: a total is one call without group_by, so add group_by only when the question asks for a ranking or a month-by-month breakdown.

tool.title: Get income statement
tool.description:
Purpose: Get the company's income statement (profit and loss) for one date range: revenue, expenses, operating income, non-operating income, taxes and net income. Use group_by=department for the GAAP P&L; group_by=category is the default.
Not for: Balances on a date (get_balance_sheet) or cash movement (get_cash_flow). One category on its own; the full statement always comes back.
Returns: start_date and end_date are the exact inclusive dates used, with currency, refreshed_at, operating_income_cents and net_income_cents, plus one top-level field per section: revenue, expenses and non_operating_income always, and uncategorized_income and taxes only when the company has those rows. With category grouping, uncategorized_expenses is also present when the company has that row. The response echoes group_by. With category grouping, each section has total_cents and categories. Each category has category_id, name, amount_cents, position and parent_category_id. Amounts are signed integer cents: income is positive and expenses are negative, so divide by 100 for dollars.
Department grouping: Expenses have total_cents and rows instead of categories. Each row has row_id, parent_row_id, kind (department, category, or group), nullable department_id and category_id, name, amount_cents and position. Parent amounts include their children. No Department is an assignment group, not uncategorized expenses. Revenue, non-operating income, optional uncategorized income and taxes keep their category format. Department grouping has no top-level uncategorized_expenses field, requires the departments feature and returns refreshed_at=null.
When to use: "What was our net income last quarter?", "How much revenue did we make in September?", "What are our biggest expenses this year?"
Dates and source: Calendar dates use America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time), and both boundaries are honored exactly, inclusive. With category grouping, whole months use whole-month rollups. Current-month start through today uses fresh month-to-date (MTD) rollups, keeping month-aligned month-to-date and year-to-date requests fast. Other partial months, including a midmonth start, use slower raw-entry reads for just those months. Stale or unfilled MTD safely falls back to raw entries; the report's numerical semantics are unchanged.
Category freshness: refreshed_at covers the entire report, including partial months. For rollup-only reads it is the maximum contributing rollup timestamp, including MTD. Any live raw portion is current as of the call, even when no raw entries match. It is null only when no contributing timestamp or live raw read is available.
Workflow: Omit both dates for the current quarter to date in Pacific Time. One call covers one period; for a month-by-month view, call once per month.
